title: APPROVAL TO DECLARE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT PROPERTIES LOCATED IN THE WILMINGTON AREA AS SURPLUS PROPERTY AND AUTHORIZE DISPOSAL
text:
RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVAL TO DECLARE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT PROPERTIES LOCATED IN THE WILMINGTON AREA AS SURPLUS PROPERTY AND AUTHORIZE DISPOSAL

Transmittal 2

Transmittal 4
Transmittal 5
Summary
: Staff requests the Board of Harbor Commissioners (Board) find and declare twenty-nine non-contiguous City of Los Angeles (City) Harbor Department (Harbor Department) parcel groups located in the East Wilmington area as “surplus property”, an additional seven non-contiguous parcel groups in the same area as “exempt surplus property”, and the Eubank site located on 826 Eubank Ave in Wilmington as surplus property. The proposed surplus sale advances the Harbor Department's Strategic Plan Objective 3: Improved Financial Performance of Port Assets, Initiative 3 - Ensure that Port properties are revenue efficient. These parcel groups (Properties) were not part of the original lands granted by the State of California under the State Tidelands Trust Grant (Tidelands Trust) but were acquired utilizing funds generated from those assets between 1980 through the early 2000s for potential future development which never transpired. Maintenance costs exceed the revenue generated from the Properties. Staff has concluded that disposal of the surplus lands is the best course of action due to the scattered locations, minimal revenue, and lack of contribution towards the Harbor Department’s obligations under the Tidelands Trust. The proposed surplus sale process will be subject to terms, conditions and procedures prescribed in Division 7 Chapter 1 Article 4 of the Los Angeles Administrative Code (LAAC), Section 7.21 et seq., the City of Los Angeles Charter Section 385, the California Surplus Land Act and all applicable laws. The Harbor Department is financially responsible for expenditures associated with the initial declaration of real property as exempt surplus and surplus property including appraising the Properties to determine the fair-market value. Appraisal costs are estimated to be approximately $296,000. Staff plans to return with the proposed Ordinance, Notice of Sale, and planned action for existing tenants once the preliminary information is obtained.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article III, Class 12 of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) 4ind and declare that the twenty-nine properties located within the East Wilmington area are surplus lands, since the Properties are no longer needed for the use of the Harbor Department and public interest and necessity requires the sale; 3) find and declare that the seven properties located within the East Wilmington area are exempt surplus lands, since each of the seven properties are less than 5,000 square feet and the Properties are no longer needed for the use of the Harbor Department and public interest and necessity requires the sale. Accessor Parcel Numbers 7428-034-903, 7428-034-904, 7428-035-901, 7428-035-917, 7428-025-901, 7428-024-907, 7428-023-900; 4) find and declare the Eubank site located at 826 Eubank Ave in Wilmington (Accessor Parcel No. 7428-019-903) as surplus land, since the property is no longer needed for the use of the Harbor Department and public interest and necessity requires the sale; 5) direct staff to comply with Division 7 Chapter 1 Article 4 of the Los Angeles Administrative Code (LAAC), LAAC Section 7.21 et seq., the City of Los Angeles Charter Section 385, and all applicable laws; and 6) adopt Resolution No. ____________.
Environmental Management
summary: Declares 29 groups of Harbor Department parcels in East Wilmington surplus, 7 more groups exempt surplus, and the Eubank Ave site surplus, clearing them for eventual sale after appraisal.
